Title: 5 ways brand lift studies can inform your campaign strategy

URL Source: https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/brand-lift-studies

Published Time: 2021-12-13T19:19:49+00:00

Markdown Content:
Before running any digital campaign, it’s crucial to align brand messaging and strategy. Doing this helps marketers ensure that a brand is portrayed in a way that is appealing to its target audience. Ultimately, this alignment encourages engagement that will drive consumers closer to the bottom of the marketing funnel.

Data-driven insights are one way that marketers can help achieve this alignment. Metrics like impressions and click-throughs are a go-to for campaign management. But aligning brand messaging and strategy goes beyond those metrics. A tactic that marketers are increasingly leveraging to gain audience insights and identify the impact of their campaigns is running a brand lift study.

## What is a brand lift study

A brand lift study measures the impact of your campaigns across all your programmatic channels. It typically will provide a picture of the consumer sentiment and brand affinity of people who have been exposed to your media.

It can be used to measure the impact of upper funnel campaigns on your consumers’ perception of your brand, but it’s also effective when it comes to mid- to lower funnel campaigns, for measuring consideration or purchase intent.

There are a couple different ways that brand lift studies can be run, but they usually revolve around a survey. The study leverages a methodology to gather feedback from consumers in the real world using a survey. Your defined “exposed” and “control” groups are asked one specific question, or a series of questions. Your “exposed” group is a group of users who have seen your ad in the past, and your “control” group is a group of users who have not seen your ad.

## Measure the impact of your campaigns

Brand lift studies go beyond traditional metrics, like impressions, to help you measure a campaign’s impact on [consumer perceptions and behaviour](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/how-agencies-thrive-podcast-episode-11/). Let’s say an athleisure brand has just launched its first marketing campaign around a new shoe line. The brand is known for its apparel, so it runs a brand lift study to understand whether the target audience is interested in the new shoes.

The study can discover how likely a consumer is to purchase the brand’s new shoes, the perception a consumer has about the brand after seeing an ad for shoes, or what brand comes to mind when a consumer thinks about that shoe style.

By identifying the target consumer’s awareness, perception, consideration and likelihood of purchase, marketers can better judge the effectiveness of a campaign. Then, marketers can use those insights to inform their digital strategy moving forward.

## Use ad creatives for insights into your audience

[Interactive ad creatives](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/benefits-of-interactive-ads/) can serve as a great tool for gathering helpful and voluntary feedback from users. These are usually referred to as survey ads, discovery ads or brand lift ads. Survey ads use an HTML5 format to create an interactive unit for users. This format captures audience responses by presenting questions. By way of buttons, a checklist or a dropdown menu, there are countless insights an advertiser can gain through a survey ad.

For example, a marketer in the [travel industry](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/travel-and-tourism-marketing/) can use survey ads to determine traveller readiness. The interactive creative can survey users to find out how willing people are to book a trip or when they would be ready to book in the future. The marketer can then rely on these insights to understand the best time to invest in a travel campaign.

Survey ads are also useful for informing decisions about new products and understanding how well they will resonate with the target audience. For example, a razor company could use a survey ad to gather data about what colors their target audience prefers when it comes to the razor’s handle.

Survey ads can be run in advance of a large campaign to help inform it. By gathering preemptive insights about the receptiveness and preferences of a target audience, marketers can create campaigns that cater best to that audience.

## 5 ways a brand lift study can inform your campaign strategy

1.   **Provides New Metrics**  
Brand lift will show you incrementality through metrics like brand awareness, ad recall, brand favourability, and brand affinity.
2.   **Determines Perception of Your Brand**  
Brand lift helps uncover how your ads impact perception of your product or brand, enabling you to adjust and optimize your campaigns.
3.   **Demystifies Your Audience**  
With brand lift, you can learn what your audience considers most important about your brand, and leverage that information to optimize messaging.
4.   **Retarget and Reach New Audiences**  
The insights from brand lift can be leveraged to create retargeting pools based on consumer responses, and build lookalike audience.
5.   **Inform Your Future Campaigns**  
Brand lift lets you know what your audience truly wants, information that can be used to optimize future campaigns and achieve your marketing objectives.

## Measuring the entire user journey with brand lift

Brand lift studies are useful for measuring the entire user journey, from upper funnel, to mid and lower funnel. Measuring the effectiveness of touch points through the customer journey is key to helping you paint a complete picture of the buying process, and to uncover ways that the process can be improved or streamlined.

If using brand lift to measure the upper funnel, you might craft the study around questions that ask whether a user recalls seeing an ad for the brand in question in the last 14 days, or you may ask them what brand they associate most with.

For the mid to lower funnel, a brand lift study can ask more granular questions. For example, you could ask how the user would describe their overall opinion of the brand, whether they would recommend the brand to a friend, or how likely they are to make a purchase form that brand.

*   [Watch this webinar](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/webinars/chat-gpt-marketing-strategy) to get expert-backed tips on building a ChatGPT advertising strategy.
*   Explore StackAdapt’s [AI-powered advertising and orchestration platform](https://www.stackadapt.com/platform) and [sign up to start using it today](https://www.stackadapt.com/sign-up).

## Brand lift study FAQs

Here are answers to some of the most commonly asked questions about brand lift studies, and how to use them.

### What do brand lift studies measure?

Brand lift studies are used to measure the impact of a digital advertising campaign for a brand. They are typically used for measuring changes in consumer perceptions of a brand after seeing an upper funnel campaign, but they’re also effective when it comes to mid- to lower funnel campaigns, for measuring consideration or purchase intent.

### What is a brand lift study?

A brand lift study measures the impact of a digital advertising campaign across all programmatic channels used. It provides insight into the consumer sentiment and brand affinity of people who have been exposed to the campaign. There are different ways that brand lift studies can be run, but they usually leverage a survey that uses a methodology to gather feedback from consumers in the real world.

### Why run a brand lift study?

Running a brand lift study helps marketers to uncover how ad campaigns impact the consumer perceptions of a product or brand. They are worth running because they enable marketers to adjust and optimize their campaigns, to achieve the best possible results.

## It’s time to use brand lift tactics

Brand lift studies and interactive ads are valuable tactics for informing your digital strategy. They can prove not just the effectiveness of a campaign, but they can provide preemptive insights into what a target audience actually wants.

These insights are an essential part of competing in today’s media landscape because they go beyond basic measurements like impressions and views to evaluate digital’s contributions with more complex performance metrics. By learning what a brand or product’s audience has to say, you can better align your media plan with a brand’s message.

[Watch our webinar](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/webinars/measure-campaign-success-with-brand-lift/) to learn more about how you can leverage brand lift studies in your digital strategy, watch our webinar.

# About A/B testing for Meta Ads

Chat with Meta AI business assistant for support around the clock Still need help? Your business assistant can help resolve account issues and unblock your business.

Start chat

A/B testing enables you to compare two versions of an ad strategy by changing variables such as ad images, ad text, audience or placement. Each version is shown to a segment of your audience, ensuring nobody sees both, then the test determines which version performs best. Running an A/B test helps you decide which ad strategy to use.

Before you select a variable to test, choose a [hypothesis for your test](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2358258211160819). For example, you might hypothesize that a custom audience strategy will outperform an interest-based audience strategy for your business.

## How A/B testing works in Meta Ads Manager

To create an A/B test, you can either duplicate an existing campaign, ad set or ad and change a variable, or compare two existing campaigns or ad sets. If you choose to duplicate an existing campaign, your ad budget is also duplicated. Otherwise, your current ad budgets are used, which you can change in Meta Ads Manager at the ad set level. Use the same budget for both versions in a test to ensure a fair comparison. A/B testing can then measure the performance of each strategy on a cost per result basis or cost per conversion lift basis.

## When to use an A/B test for your Meta ads

We recommend A/B testing when you’re trying to measure changes to your advertising or quickly compare two strategies. We do not recommend testing informally, such as by turning ad sets or campaigns on and off manually. Informal testing can lead to inefficient ad delivery and unreliable test results. For example, A/B testing helps ensure your audiences will be evenly split and statistically comparable, while informal testing can lead to overlapping audiences.

You can [create an A/B test in Meta Ads Manager](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/355670925639619) or in the [**Experiments** tool](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/3506622486044209). Learn more about the [ways to create an A/B test](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1159714227408868).

results.title: Bringing clarity to Connected TV attribution: Techniques and innovations
results.markdown:
Title: Bringing clarity to Connected TV attribution: Techniques and innovations

URL Source: https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/connected-tv-attribution

Published Time: 2025-02-06T11:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
As [connected TV (CTV)](https://www.stackadapt.com/connected-tv-advertising) continues to grow as a dominant force in advertising, it offers brands unparalleled opportunities to engage audiences in more targeted and impactful ways. Yet, one critical question lingers: _How do we measure the real impact of CTV campaigns?_

[Measurement](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/ctv-measurement) and [attribution](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/what-is-marketing-attribution) are among the most crucial—and challenging—frontiers in unlocking the full potential of CTV advertising. According to recent data, advertisers are aware of this, with [86% prioritizing reach and frequency](https://chart-na1.emarketer.com/268178/importance-of-select-reporting-metrics-connected-tv-ctvott-advertising-according-us-ctvott-advertisers-april-2024-of-respondents) and 85% emphasizing [brand lift](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/stackadapt-brand-lift-study) as important reporting metrics. However, metrics like sales lift (84%) and website visit attribution (77%) illustrate a growing focus on connecting campaign performance to tangible business outcomes.

This article explores how new tools and techniques tackle these challenges head-on. From tracking cross-device activity to connecting online impressions with offline actions, we’ll unpack the strategies that will help you prove the value of your campaigns and optimize them for greater impact.

## Understanding CTV attribution

CTV attribution refers to the process of determining how [CTV advertising](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/integrate-connected-tv) campaigns influence consumer actions and contribute to business outcomes. It bridges the gap between ad exposure and measurable results, such as website visits, app downloads, or in-store purchases.

Unlike [traditional TV advertising](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/linear-tv-vs-connected-tv), which often relies on broad audience metrics, CTV attribution allows advertisers to track more specific behaviours, connecting the dots between an ad and its impact on the bottom line.

CTV attribution typically involves collecting data from various sources to create a clear picture of viewer interactions. This includes tracking ad impressions on CTV devices, integrating [1st-](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/1st-party-data) and [3rd-party data](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/third-party-audiences), and analyzing user actions across multiple channels and devices.

For example, if a consumer sees a CTV ad and later visits the advertiser’s website or completes a purchase, attribution models can link those actions back to the original ad exposure.

Advanced tools often use household-level data, cross-device tracking, and machine learning to refine the accuracy of these insights.

Focusing on attribution is essential because it helps advertisers understand the actual value of their campaigns. CTV’s ability to target specific audiences makes it a highly efficient advertising channel, but without proper attribution, businesses may struggle to justify their investments.

Demonstrating a clear connection between ad exposure and [key performance indicators (KPIs)](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/programmatic-kpis-explained) such as sales or engagement builds confidence in the channel’s effectiveness. Additionally, robust attribution allows advertisers to optimize their [CTV strategies](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/connected-tv-marketing-strategies) by identifying which campaigns, creatives, or placements drive the most impact, leading to more informed decisions and better returns on ad spend.

## Attribution models for Connected TV

Understanding the different attribution models used in CTV advertising is key to evaluating campaign performance and making data-driven decisions. Each model approaches the question of “what led to the conversion?” differently, offering distinct benefits and limitations.

### First-touch attribution

This model gives 100% credit to a viewer’s first interaction with a CTV ad or campaign. For example, if a consumer sees a brand’s CTV ad and later visits its website after other touchpoints like social media or email, the CTV ad is considered solely responsible for driving the conversion.

*   **Strengths**: Ideal for understanding which campaigns generate initial interest and awareness. It’s simple to implement and provides clear insights into top-of-funnel performance.
*   **Weaknesses**: Ignores the influence of subsequent interactions that may have contributed to the final conversion, leading to an incomplete picture of the customer journey.

### Last-touch attribution

This model attributes 100% of the credit to the final interaction before the conversion. For instance, if a consumer sees a CTV ad, clicks on a paid search ad days later, and completes a purchase, the search ad would receive full credit.

*   **Strengths**: Highlights the last step in the conversion funnel, helping advertisers understand which touchpoint directly drives actions like purchases or sign-ups.
*   **Weaknesses**: Oversimplifies the journey by disregarding earlier touchpoints, potentially undervaluing the role of CTV in building awareness and nurturing interest.

### Multi-touch attribution

Multi-touch attribution spreads credit across all touchpoints in a consumer’s journey. For example, if a viewer sees a CTV ad, clicks on a social media ad, and finally receives an email prompting the purchase, each interaction is assigned a proportionate share of credit.

*   **Strengths**: Provides a holistic view of how various touchpoints work together, making it easier to optimize cross-channel campaigns. It’s particularly useful in complex, [multi-channel advertising strategies](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/downloads/guide-to-multi-channel-advertising).
*   **Weaknesses**: It can be challenging to implement due to its reliance on robust data collection and sophisticated modelling. Assigning weights to each touchpoint can also be subjective.

### View-through attribution

This model credits a conversion to a CTV ad even if the consumer did not click on it, as long as they were exposed to it and later completed the desired action. For example, if someone sees a CTV ad for a fitness brand and buys a product online days later without clicking a direct link, the view-through model credits the ad exposure.

*   **Strengths**: Captures the impact of passive exposure, which is critical for CTV campaigns that don’t rely on direct clicks. It reflects how top-of-funnel activity influences conversions.
*   **Weaknesses**: Correlation doesn’t always mean causation; unrelated factors could have influenced the conversion, making it harder to prove a direct connection.

### The micro-conversion revolution

While traditional attribution focuses on the final conversion (e.g., a purchase), the micro-conversion revolution emphasizes smaller, incremental actions that indicate progress along the customer journey. Micro-conversions include visiting a landing page, adding a product to a cart, or signing up for a newsletter after viewing a CTV ad. These micro-actions provide richer insights into consumer behaviour and how CTV ads move prospects closer to the ultimate conversion.

This approach is gaining traction because it enables advertisers to optimize campaigns in real time by identifying and focusing on high-value touchpoints earlier in the funnel.

Selecting the right attribution model often depends on the campaign’s goals and the available data. A combination of models tailored to specific objectives can help advertisers get the most comprehensive view of their CTV campaign performance.

## Benefits and advantages of CTV attribution

CTV attribution provides advertisers the tools to bridge the gap between ad exposure and measurable business outcomes. Below are the key advantages of implementing a robust CTV attribution approach.

### Accurate attribution for performance clarity

Attribution frameworks help establish a clear link between CTV ad exposure and online engagement. Rather than relying on traditional TV metrics, advertisers can track how CTV influences website visits, conversions, and other key actions. This level of accuracy ensures a more precise understanding of campaign impact.

### Enhanced tracking across devices

With consumers engaging across multiple screens, cross-device tracking is essential. Advanced identity resolution technology connects CTV impressions to user actions across mobile, desktop, and other devices. This ensures a more complete and unified view of the customer journey.

### Optimized campaign performance

results.title: Mastering Advertising Effectiveness Measurement
results.markdown:
Title: Mastering Advertising Effectiveness Measurement

URL Source: https://adwave.com/resources/advertising-effectiveness-measurement

Published Time: 2025-11-15T00:00:00+00:00

Markdown Content:
So, what do we mean when we talk about measuring ad effectiveness? It's simply the process of figuring out if your ad campaigns are doing what you want them to do. It’s about drawing a clear line from the money you spend on ads to the results your business sees, making sure you’re not just shouting into the void but actively moving the needle.

This means tracking the right numbers to understand both how many people your ads are reaching and, more importantly, how those ads are changing what people do.

![Image 1: A person pointing at a colorful chart showing advertising data and analytics.](https://media.adwave.com/fia320z3blxi/2rhBzMhCEYwu5Ow4gm4vFi/a66cd64b8dc391f6a70ba9518c2e8605/b946b3e6-3c92-4526-b792-b827f6fe0db0.jpg)
Let’s be honest for a second. A huge chunk of advertising money gets spent with very little idea of what's working. For too many businesses, advertising feels like throwing a bunch of stuff at a wall to see what sticks. This "spray and pray" approach is a recipe for wasted money, missed chances, and stagnant growth.

Think about it like a chef creating a new recipe. A good chef doesn't just throw ingredients in a pot, serve it up, and hope for the best. They taste and tweak as they go, a little more salt, a bit less heat. They’re constantly getting feedback. **Advertising effectiveness measurement** is the marketing equivalent of tasting the soup. It's about analyzing your campaign's entire "recipe," from the very first ad impression all the way to the final sale.

### From Guesswork to a Growth Engine

Without a solid measurement system, you're flying blind. Sure, sales might have gone up last month, but can you confidently say your ads were the reason? What if it was just a seasonal bump, a competitor's stumble, or a random TikTok that went viral? This is precisely why real measurement is a business necessity.

It allows you to:

*   **Stop guessing:** Base your next move on hard data, not gut feelings.

*   **Avoid wasted budget:** Quickly spot the channels or ads that are duds and shift that money elsewhere.

*   **Double down on winners:** Identify exactly what’s driving results so you can invest more in what works.

This data-first mindset is a world away from the old-school methods. The whole field has evolved from simple "Do you remember this ad?" surveys in the 1950s to much more sophisticated tracking. A big leap forward was the Millward Brown Institute's Advanced Tracking Programme back in **1976**, which started to continuously measure how advertising affected consumer choices over time. This history laid the groundwork for the powerful, yet accessible, strategies we have today, like those used for [measuring TV advertising effectiveness](https://adwave.com/why-tv-works/), which we'll dig into next.

![Image 2: A close-up shot of a digital dashboard on a tablet displaying various advertising performance metrics like CPM, Reach, and Conversions, with colorful graphs and charts.](https://media.adwave.com/fia320z3blxi/1BoKWhwYXJvhVCq7KJeAh3/7f8a6324d19c9822c9ab69b4b20b723f/02deab92-c73e-49ca-b439-0ee018a2bd5a.jpg)
So, how do you know if an ad campaign is working? You have to learn to speak the language of metrics. These are the specific data points that turn abstract goals like "brand awareness" into hard numbers you can work with.

Think of it like this: if your ad campaign is a car on a road trip, the metrics are the gauges on your dashboard. They tell you your speed, your fuel level, and if the engine is overheating. Without them, you’re just driving blind.

You can group most of these vital signs into two main buckets. First, you have **reach metrics**, which tell you how many people you’re getting in front of. Second, there are **impact metrics**, which show whether seeing your ad made a real difference.

### Measuring Your Campaign's Reach

Reach metrics answer a simple but important question: "Is anyone out there?" Before you can persuade someone, you first have to get their attention.

Let’s go old school for a second. Imagine you’re handing out flyers for a new local shop.

*   **Reach** would be the total number of unique people who get one of your flyers.

*   **Frequency** is the average number of times a single person ends up with your flyer.

*   **CPM (Cost Per Mille)** is the money you spent to get **1,000** flyers into people's hands.

The same logic applies perfectly to digital and TV advertising. A low CPM is great, it means you're efficiently getting your message out there. But a super high frequency might signal you're just annoying a small group of people over and over.

This balance is especially important today, with audience targeting becoming a huge factor in TV advertising, which has seen a massive surge in [ad-supported viewership in recent years](https://adwave.com/resources/us-tv-ad-supported-share-q2-2025/).

### Measuring Your Campaign's Impact

Getting your ad seen is one thing, but making it count is another. This is where impact metrics come in. They help you answer the most important question of all: "Did the ad _work_?"

An ad can reach millions of people, but if it doesn't change what they think or do, it’s just expensive noise.

> An ad’s success isn't just about being seen; it's about being effective. Impact metrics separate the campaigns that just spend money from the ones that make money.

These metrics zero in on how your audience responds _after_ they see your ad.

*   **Viewability:** This one is just common sense. Did a real person see the ad? An ad that loads at the bottom of a webpage that no one ever scrolls to has zero viewability and, therefore, zero chance of making an impact.

*   **Brand Lift:** This is all about perception. It measures the change in how consumers see your brand after the campaign. Are more people aware of you now? Do they associate you with quality?

*   **Conversions:** For many businesses, this is the bottom line. It’s the specific action you wanted someone to take, making a purchase, signing up for a demo, or downloading a guide.

No single metric can give you the full picture. A successful campaign finds the sweet spot between efficient reach and measurable impact.

To help you get a handle on these terms, here's a quick breakdown of the core metrics you'll encounter and what they're best used for.

### Key Advertising Performance Metrics Explained

Getting comfortable with this vocabulary is the first step toward understanding what’s really driving your results and how to steer your strategy in the right direction.

## Choosing the Right Measurement Framework

Think of individual metrics like the notes in a piece of music. They're essential, but they only tell part of the story. To really understand how your ads are performing, you need a framework, a complete composition that brings all those notes together. These frameworks are like different lenses, each giving you a unique perspective on your campaign's success.

Picking the right lens comes down to the question you’re trying to answer. Are you just wondering which ad creative works best? Or are you trying to prove that your ads are _causing_ sales, not just getting credit for them? Different questions need different tools. Let’s walk through four powerful frameworks, starting with the most straightforward and moving to the most detailed, to help you master **advertising effectiveness measurement**.

### The Scientific Method of Advertising

The simplest, most direct way to measure impact is with **A/B testing** (also called split testing) and **holdout tests**. This is basically the scientific method applied to marketing. You create a couple of versions of an ad (changing just one thing like the headline, image, or call-to-action) and show them to different segments of your audience to see which one gets better results.

A holdout test takes this a step further. You show your ad to one group (the test group) and then deliberately show nothing to a similar group (the holdout, or control group). By comparing what the two groups do, you can isolate the true impact of your advertising. It’s a clean, direct way to get causal evidence of what’s working, cutting right through the guesswork.

Digital platforms have made this kind of experimentation, known as randomized control trials (RCTs), the gold standard for measurement. It's a huge leap from older models, as digital tools let us run precise experiments at the user level, establishing cause-and-effect with far more confidence. You can even [read more about these experimental methods](https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w19520/w19520.pdf) and how major tech companies use them to get precise ROI estimates.

In this example, Version B is the clear winner, showing how a single change can directly influence user behavior
